name: Rajab
intro:
The month of Rajab is full of memorable and unforgettable occasions. On one hand, it contains the birthdays of the Imams (AS) and the Prophet's (SAWW) appointment to prophethood (Bi'tha); on the other, the deaths of several well-known enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS). These are joyful tidings that make this month a month of delight. The martyrdoms of the Infallibles (AS) and of several of their loyal companions also make this month a time of mourning for the Family of Muhammad (AS).
On days 1, 2, 3, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28 and 29 of Rajab, fresh memories are revived, which we review below.
The births of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), Imam al-Baqir (AS), Imam al-Jawad (AS), Imam Ali al-Naqi (AS) and Hazrat Ali Asghar (AS) are continuous blessings sent down in this month. The Bi'tha of the Prophet (SAWW), the departure from the Valley (Shi'b) of Abu Talib (AS), and the granting of Fadak to Hazrat Zahra (AS) are events of special importance from the standpoint of belief. The deaths of Mu'awiya, al-Ma'mun and al-Mu'tamid the Abbasid are also days of joy for the friends of the Ahl al-Bayt.
The martyrdom of Hazrat Zahra (AS) according to one account, as well as the martyrdoms of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) and Imam al-Hadi (AS), are days of tears and grief in this month. The passing of Hazrat Zaynab (AS), Hazrat Abu Talib (AS), Hazrat Khadija (AS), Ibrahim the son of the Prophet (SAWW), and the Najashi (Negus), the king of Abyssinia, are counted among the sorrowful events of this month.
In addition, the attack on Imam Mujtaba (AS) at Mada'in and the departure of Imam Husayn (AS) from Medina toward Mecca are two important events of this month.
The first congregational prayer in Islam, the Muslims' migration to Abyssinia and their return, the change of the Qibla, the conquest of Khaybar at the hands of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), the Nakhla expedition, the entry of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) into Kufa, the first sermon of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) in the Mosque of Kufa, the start of the ill-fated caliphate of Yazid, and the flight of Abu Bakr and Umar in the Battle of Khaybar are other pages of Islamic history that took place in the month of Rajab.

events.title: Visiting Imam Husayn (AS)
events.text: On the night and day of the first of this month, visiting Mawlana al-Shahid Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (AS) is recommended. It is narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that he said: ((Whoever visits Imam Husayn (AS) on the first day of Rajab, Almighty God will forgive his sins.)) If visiting that Imam is not possible for someone on this day, they should visit the other holy shrines of the Infallibles (AS), and if even that is not possible for them, they should express their devotion by greeting those honored tombs from afar.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 16. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 293.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 34.

events.title: Birth of Imam al-Baqir (AS)
events.text:
Hazrat Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Baqir al-'Ulum (AS) was born in Medina on Friday, the first of Rajab, in the year 57 AH. His birth has also been mentioned on the 3rd and 6th of Safar and on the 5th and 22nd of Rajab. His blessed name was Muhammad, his kunya Abu Ja'far, and his titles were Baqir al-'Ulum, al-Shakir lillah, Hadi, Amin and Shabih. The last title is due to his resemblance to the Prophet (SAWW).
His honorable father was Hazrat Imam Zayn al-'Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), and his mother was Umm Abdillah Fatima, the daughter of Imam Hasan Mujtaba (AS). Imam al-Baqir (AS) is the first Alawid whose noble lineage reaches, through both father and mother, to the Prophet (SAWW), Amir al-Mu'minin and Hazrat Zahra (AS). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said about Umm Abdillah: ((She was among the believing, God-fearing and righteous women.)) In another narration Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said: ((Among the children of Imam Hasan (AS), there was none like her.)) It suffices for the greatness and nobility of this lady that she was present at the event of Karbala with Hazrat Sayyid al-Sajidin Ali ibn al-Husayn and Baqir al-'Ulum (AS), was taken into captivity along with those honored figures, Zaynab al-Kubra and the other members of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), and witnessed the events of Kufa and Syria.

events.title: Birth of Imam Ali al-Naqi (AS)
events.text: According to one account, the birth of Imam al-Hadi (AS) took place on this day. Other accounts of his birth are 15 Dhu al-Hijja, 5 Rajab, 27 Jumada al-Akhira and 3 Rajab; the details are given under 15 Dhu al-Hijja.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 18.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam al-Hadi (AS)
events.text:
The martyrdom of Imam Ali al-Naqi (AS) in the year 254 AH, according to the well-known view, occurred at the age of 41. The late Kulayni reported his martyrdom as being on 26 Jumada al-Akhira. It is well known that he was 6 or 8 years and 5 months old when his honorable father, Jawad al-A'imma (AS), was martyred, and the duration of that noble figure's Imamate was 33 years.
The days of Imam al-Hadi's (AS) life coincided with the unjust caliphates of al-Ma'mun, al-Mu'tasim, al-Wathiq, al-Mutawakkil, al-Muntasir, al-Musta'in and al-Mu'tazz, may God curse them; and finally al-Mu'tazz martyred him with poison.
The blessed lifespan of that Imam was 41 years and a few months; he lived 13 years in Medina and spent the rest of his Imamate in Samarra by the compulsion of al-Mutawakkil. The governor of Medina wrote to al-Mutawakkil: "If you have any need of Mecca and Medina, remove Ali ibn Muhammad (AS) from this land, for he has made everyone obedient to himself." In Medina, on al-Mutawakkil's orders, the means of harassing and harming the Imam were multiplied, until they took him to Samarra, where they showed him disrespect, until al-Mu'tazz martyred him.
Imam al-'Askari (AS) performed his washing, shrouding and prayer; later, outwardly, these rites were carried out by others, and they buried him in his own house, at the present location of the holy shrine.

events.title: Birth of Imam al-Jawad (AS)
events.text:
Hazrat Jawad al-A'imma (AS), according to the well-known view, was born on the tenth of the month of Rajab in the year 195 AH. Other accounts of his birth are: 17 Ramadan, 15 Ramadan, the end of Dhu al-Qa'da; and according to one account, his birth took place on 13 Rajab.
His honorable father was Imam Reza (AS), and his mother was Lady Sabika or Durra, whom Hazrat Reza (AS) named ((Khayzuran)).
His name was Muhammad, his kunya Abu Ja'far, and his most famous titles are Taqi and Jawad. Hazrat Reza (AS) used to refer to him by his kunya and would say: ((Abu Ja'far has written me a letter)); the letters that reached him from that Imam were of utmost dignity and beauty, and when the Imam (AS) wished to write a letter to Imam al-Jawad (AS), he addressed him with greatness and respect. One day, in the days of Hazrat Jawad's (AS) childhood, he was brought to his honorable father, Imam Reza (AS). The Imam said: ((This is a newborn than whom none more blessed for the Shi'a has ever been born)), because more than forty years and a few months of Imam Reza's (AS) blessed life had passed and he still had no child, and some of the Shi'a were worried about the matter of the Imamate; when God granted Jawad al-A'imma (AS) to our master Hazrat Reza (AS), the people's worry, doubt and hesitation were removed.
He had six children: Abu al-Hasan Hazrat Hadi (AS), Abu Talib Zayd, Abu Ja'far Musa Mubarraqa, Hakima Khatun, Khadija Khatun and Umm Kulthum.

events.title: Birth of Hazrat Ali Asghar (AS)
events.text:
The blessed birth of Hazrat Bab al-Hawa'ij Ali Asghar (AS) took place on this day. Considering that he was martyred at six months of age on the day of Ashura in Karbala, his birth corresponds to this day. Some have also recorded his birth on the 8th or 9th.
His noble name was Abdullah, known as Ali Asghar. His noble titles are Bab al-Hawa'ij, al-Radi' (the Infant), and "the one slaughtered from ear to ear." His honorable father was Imam Husayn (AS), and his exalted mother was Hazrat Rubab, the daughter of Imru' al-Qays al-Kalbi.
His killer was the accursed Harmala ibn Kahil al-Asadi, who burned the heart of Imam Husayn (AS), the Ahl al-Bayt and the Shi'a, indeed of every listener to this tragedy.
sources: Taqwim al-A'imma (AS): pp. 73–78. Sahab-e Rahmat: p. 535.

events.title: Death of Mu'awiya
events.text: On this day in the year 60 AH, Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, may God curse him, at the age of 78, hastened in Syria to the depths of Hell. It is a day of joy for the people of faith and of grief and sorrow for the people of disbelief and tyranny. Fasting on this day is recommended as thanksgiving to God for Mu'awiya's destruction.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 34. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 316.

subsections.title: Lineage of Mu'awiya
subsections.text:
Kalbi the genealogist and Ibn Ruzbihan, who are considered trustworthy by Sunni scholars, have reported that Mu'awiya was the son of four men: Umara, Musafir, Abu Sufyan, and a man whose name they do not mention. Raghib Isfahani in al-Muhadarat, and Ibn Abi al-Hadid, quoting Zamakhshari's Rabi' al-Abrar, report that Mu'awiya was attributed to four people: Musafir ibn Abi Amr, Umara ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abbas, and Sabbah, who was Umara ibn al-Walid's singer. Mu'awiya's mother, Hind, had a complete fondness for Sabbah — who was a handsome youth and a worker of Abu Sufyan! But outwardly he is called Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Harb. Abu Sufyan was an ugly, short man; one of his eyes was blinded at Ta'if and the other at Yarmouk. His inner self was blinder than his eyes, and he played a role in the utmost enmity and hostility toward the Prophet (SAWW); in the year of the conquest of Mecca, out of fear, he accepted Islam and lived in hypocrisy until he went to his doom at the age of 82 in the year 30 AH.
It should not remain hidden that Hamama was one of Mu'awiya's grandmothers, who was a flag-bearer and well known in the market of Dhu al-Majaz! From this, the lineage of Abu Sufyan also becomes clear. Mu'awiya's mother was Hind, who was among the women of the red-flag houses and had great desire for black slaves; from explaining the condition of Mu'awiya's father, the condition of his mother Hind becomes clear.
Muhaddith Qummi (RH) says: Since the Prophet (SAWW), at the conquest of Mecca, considered the shedding of Mu'awiya's blood permissible, he accepted Islam five months before the Prophet's (SAWW) martyrdom, through the insistence and intercession of Abbas.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 47, 48, 50, 52. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 448–449. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rajab, p. 174.
Usd al-Ghaba: vol. 3, p. 13.
The end of the month of Dhu al-Hijja is the day of Hind's death, whose circumstances are mentioned there.

subsections.title: Mu'awiya's Rule in Syria
subsections.text:
Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan went toward Syria at the head of the Muslim army on behalf of Abu Bakr, and Mu'awiya accompanied them. Yazid died in Syria, and Abu Bakr entrusted the governorship of the Syrian provinces to Mu'awiya, and it remained so until the caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), when Mu'awiya's rebellion against him began. Thus the foundation of Mu'awiya's oppressions was also laid by Abu Bakr.
In the year 45 AH, Mu'awiya took the pledge of allegiance for his son Yazid. He was the first to promote cursing Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and at the end of the Friday prayer sermon he would curse and insult Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). He ordered this cursing to be carried out in all cities, and it continued until the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who prohibited cursing him.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 33, p. 214.

subsections.title: Mu'awiya's Enmity toward Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text:
Mu'awiya ordered the Companions and the Followers to fabricate hadiths in condemnation of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), and he martyred a large number of that Imam's lovers and devotees, such as Malik al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i, who was martyred by poison at Qulzum in Egypt. He martyred Imam Mujtaba (AS) by poisoning, through the hand of the Imam's wife, Ja'da.
Mu'awiya was a pleasure-seeking and gluttonous man, to the point that, from excessive eating, he would say: ((I am tired, but I am not full)); and this was because of the Messenger of God's (SAWW) curse upon him. He had considerable experience in hypocrisy and demagoguery. Muhaddith Qummi (RH) reports that two hundred reports have been narrated through reliable Sunni chains in condemnation of Mu'awiya.
sources: Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 2, p. 223.

subsections.title: The Story of Mu'awiya's Death
subsections.text:
Finally, on the road from Mecca to Syria, Mu'awiya fell ill, to the point that he trembled and his mouth could not be closed, until he entered Syria and there gave up his soul to the Keeper of Hell and became hostage to his own deeds. His age at death has been reported as 75, 82 or 92 years.
His crimes are more than can be contained in this summary, but at the time of death he said to one of his close associates: I have committed several great sins: I usurped the right of Ali ibn Abi Talib; I brought about the martyrdom of Hasan ibn Ali by deceiving Ja'da; I chose Yazid as my successor; and I had Hujr ibn Adi and his companions killed. Regarding the death of Mu'awiya, some have mentioned only the month, some have given 4 Rajab and others 22 Rajab. 12 Rajab, 14 Rajab and 15 Rajab have also been reported, and these three views are closer to one another.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 449. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rajab, p. 173.

events.title: Entry of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) into Kufa
events.text: On this day in the year 36 AH, after the Battle of the Camel, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) entered Kufa and chose that city as the seat of his government, and on this day he delivered his first sermon in the city of Kufa.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, pp. 118–178. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 104. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 32, p. 352.

events.title: Birth of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
events.text: The first Imam of the believers and the immediate vicegerent of God after the Messenger of God, the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), his brother, cousin, minister and son-in-law, the master of the successors, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), was born on Friday, 13 Rajab, in the Sacred House of God, inside the revered Ka'ba — a place where no child was born before him or after him, nor ever will be. His noble name is Ali (AS). The author of Kitab al-Anwar says: Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) has 300 names in the Book of God. His most famous title is Amir al-Mu'minin, and Ibn Shahr Ashub has recorded more than 850 titles for him.
sources: Irshad of Mufid: vol. 1, p. 5. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 306. Tahdhib of Shaykh Tusi: vol. 6, p. 19. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 599. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 383. Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 3, p. 353. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 21.

Al-Hakim says in al-Mustadrak: The reports are mutawatir (widely transmitted) that Fatima bint Asad (AS) gave birth to Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) inside the Ka'ba: vol. 3, p. 483. Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim Dihlawi, known as Shah Wali (the father of Abd al-Aziz Dihlawi, who wrote the book al-Tuhfa al-Ithna 'Ashariyya), says in the book Izalat al-Khafa': The reports are mutawatir that Fatima bint Asad (AS) gave birth to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) inside the Ka'ba on Friday, 13 Rajab, 30 years after the Year of the Elephant, and that no one before him or after him was born in that place. al-Ghadir: vol. 6, p. 22. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 21. The statements of the great Shi'a scholars on this subject are more than can be mentioned in this summary. subsections.title: Titles of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text: His most famous kunya is Abu al-Hasan (AS). In addition to the names and titles that he has in the various heavenly books in various languages... he is known among the people of the heavens as Shamsatil. On earth he is Jamha'il; on the Tablet (Lawh) he is Qansum; on the Pen (Qalam) he is Mansum; on the Throne ('Arsh) he is Mu'in; with Ridwan he is Amin; with the houris he is Asab; in the Scrolls of Abraham (AS) he is Hizbil; in Hebrew he is Balqiyatis; in Syriac he is Sharuhil; in the Torah he is Ilya; in the Psalms he is Arya; in the Gospel he is Barya; in the Scrolls he is Hajar 'Ayn; in the Qur'an he is Ali.
sources: Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 3, p. 319.

subsections.title: The Parents of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text:
His exalted father was the Master of Batha', Hazrat Abu Talib (AS), and his mother was Fatima bint Asad ibn Hashim ibn Abd Manaf, the lady of the household of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS), from whose treasury of infallibility and store of modesty and chastity the lights of Imamate and Wilayah first emerged, and she was the first Hashimite woman to bring forth such a radiant star. She was not only the mother of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS); after the death of Abd al-Muttalib (AS) — when six or eight years of the Prophet's (SAWW) blessed life had passed and he had been entrusted to Abu Talib (AS) — Fatima bint Asad (AS) acted as a mother to the Prophet (SAWW), always put him before her own children, saw the signs of prophethood in him every day, and the Messenger of God (SAWW) addressed her as "Mother."
Likewise, after the passing of Hazrat Khadija al-Kubra (AS), the Prophet (SAWW) entrusted Fatima al-Zahra (AS) to Fatima bint Asad (AS). She acted as a mother to her and, in the lap of her honor, cared with heart and soul for that veiled lady of the two worlds until she herself departed this world.
She passed away in Medina in the 4th year of the Hijra and was buried in Baqi'. When Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) informed the Prophet (SAWW) of his mother's death, the Prophet said: ((She was my mother.)) Then he gave his turban and garment to shroud Fatima (AS) in them, and he himself performed the funeral prayer over her body and said forty takbirs. Then he lay down in the grave, and at the time of burial he recited the talqin for her and prayed for her.
sources: A brief account of the life of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS) is given under 26 Rajab.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 113.
Summarized from Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, pp. 3, 4, 5, 6.

subsections.title: The Light of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) in the Loins of His Forefathers
subsections.text:
The hadith of the birth of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) also points to the firmness of the faith of Fatima bint Asad (AS), his mother. The light that came from the Throne of the Lord was passed on among the prophets and their successors, one after another, until it reached Abd al-Muttalib (AS), and then that light was divided into two parts. One light was in the blessed forehead of Abdullah (AS), the honorable father of the Prophet (SAWW), which later passed to the forehead of Amina (AS) and then to the blessed face of the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW). The other half of the light was placed in the blessed forehead of Abu Talib (AS).
God granted Abu Talib (AS) several children: Aqil, Talib, Ja'far, Fakhita (or Umm Hani), Jumana, and Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). When God gave Ali (AS) to Abu Talib and Fatima bint Asad (AS), that light was shining on the face of Fatima bint Asad (AS).
sources: Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, pp. 6–7.

subsections.title: The Birthplace of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text:
The birthplace of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) is the noblest of places, namely the Haram (the Sacred Sanctuary). The noblest place in the Haram is the Mosque, and the noblest spot in the Mosque is the Ka'ba. No child other than him was born in that place — and that on the master of days, Friday, in a sacred month and in the Sacred House!!
Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) did not open his blessed eyes for three days; he was brought to the Prophet (SAWW), and it was there that he opened his eyes. The Prophet said: ((He singled me out with his gaze, and I singled him out with my knowledge.)) Then he took him into his arms and brought him to the house of Abu Talib (AS).
sources: Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 2, p. 200.
Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 2, pp. 204–205.

subsections.title: Prophecy of the Birth of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text:
Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari says: There was a monk named ((Mathram ibn Ra'ib)) who had worshipped for 190 years but had never asked God for anything. One day he asked God to show him one of His friends. Almighty God sent Abu Talib (AS) to him, and after the monk learned who this gentleman was, he gave him the glad tidings: "O Abu Talib, God will bestow upon you a son who is a friend of God, and his noble name is Ali. When you meet him, convey my greetings to him and tell him that Mathram the monk affirms the oneness of God and bears witness to your Wilayah, O Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)."
When Abu Talib (AS) left, he ate heavenly dates, grapes and pomegranates and came home. Fatima bint Asad (AS), the lady of Abu Talib's (AS) household, also ate a date that the Prophet (SAWW) had given her. The Prophet (SAWW) had said: Only one who acknowledges my monotheism and prophethood will eat this date.
After his father and mother ate the heavenly fruits, the blessed being of Hazrat Mawla al-Muwahhidin Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) came into existence. When Fatima bint Asad (AS) became pregnant with that noble being, her beauty and radiance increased.
sources: Manaqib: vol. 2, pp. 192–193, 197. Rawdat al-Wa'izin: vol. 1, p. 78.

subsections.title: The Conception of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text:
When his noble being was placed in the womb of Fatima bint Asad (AS), an earthquake struck Mecca. The Quraysh brought the idols to Mount Abu Qubays, but the earthquake grew stronger and the idols fell on their faces. They took refuge with Abu Talib (AS), who went up the mountain and said: ((O people, a great event has occurred this night. God has created a being such that, unless you obey him, acknowledge his Wilayah and bear witness to his Imamate, this earthquake will not subside. So acknowledge obedience to him, and his Wilayah and Imamate.)) Then, shedding tears, he raised his blessed hands and said: ((My Lord and my Master, I call upon You by the praiseworthy Muhammad-hood, the lofty Alawi-hood and the radiant, luminous Fatimi-hood, to bestow Your mercy and kindness upon the land of Tihama.)) The others said Amen. When the prayer ended, the earthquake stopped. In the Age of Ignorance, whenever the Arabs were in distress they would recite this prayer, and the distress would be removed.
Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (AS) heard his voice from within the mother's womb and fainted. Also, when Fatima bint Asad (AS) was going to circumambulate the House of God, he would suddenly press his two feet hard from inside the womb and would not let his mother approach the place where the idols were set up — even though his mother was circumambulating the House of God for worship. At another time, the idols would fall on their faces before that unborn child. The fierce lion of Ta'if bowed before Abu Talib (AS). When he asked it about Ali, the lion said: You are the father of the Lion of God, the helper of Muhammad, the Prophet of God (SAWW), and the guardian of the Lion of God.
sources: Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 2, pp. 196–197. Rawdat al-Wa'izin: vol. 1, p. 79. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 11.

subsections.title: The Mother of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) in the Ka'ba
subsections.text:
On the night of Friday, 13 Rajab, the noble lady of Abu Talib (AS) felt pain, but found calm by reciting a special name. When Abu Talib (AS) wanted to bring some women of the Quraysh to help Fatima bint Asad (AS), a voice came from a corner of the house: ((O Abu Talib, be patient, for an unclean hand must not touch the friend of God.))
In the morning, Fatima bint Asad (AS) heard a voice: ((O Fatima, come to Our House.)) Abu Talib (AS) and the Prophet (SAWW) brought her to the Masjid al-Haram. Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who was sitting in the mosque with a group of people, saw Fatima (AS) enter the Masjid al-Haram, stand before the Ka'ba, look toward the sky and say: ((O Lord, I believe in You, in the prophets and in the books that have come from You. I affirm the word of my grandfather Abraham the Friend, who built this House, and by the right of the child who is in my womb, who speaks to me and finds comfort with me through his speech, and whom I am certain is one of Your signs, make this birth easy for me.))
Suddenly those present in the Masjid al-Haram saw that the wall at the back, on the side of the Ka'ba, split open, and Fatima bint Asad (AS) entered. However much they tried, they could not open the lock of the Ka'ba door, and they knew that God's wisdom was at work.
Fatima bint Asad (AS) says: When I entered the Ka'ba I saw Eve, Sarah, Asiya the mother of Musa ibn Imran, and Maryam the mother of Isa come. They greeted me: "Peace be upon you, O friend of God," and sat before me.
Whatever they did at the birth of the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), they also did at the birth of Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), since Fatima bint Asad (AS) had been present at the birth of the Prophet (SAWW) and had told Abu Talib (AS) about it. Hazrat Abu Talib (AS) had previously said to her: ((Be patient for 30 years until God grants you a child like the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), except in prophethood, who will be his successor and minister.))
sources: Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 2, pp. 198–199. Amali of Shaykh Tusi: p. 706. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, pp. 8–36. Aftab-e Ka'ba: p. 45.
A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 306. Irshad: vol. 1, p. 5.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 6. Rawdat al-Wa'izin: vol. 1, p. 81.

subsections.title: The Day of the Birth of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
subsections.text:
On Friday, Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) rose like the sun upon a red stone in the right corner of the Ka'ba. As soon as he set foot on the floor of the Ka'ba, he fell into prostration, raised his hands toward the sky and said: Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa anna Muhammadan rasul Allah, wa ashhadu anna Aliyyan wali Muhammad rasul Allah, bi-Muhammadin yakhtimu Allah al-nubuwwa wa bi yakhtimu al-wasiyya wa ana Amir al-Mu'minin: ((I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad (SAWW) is the Prophet of God, and that Ali is the successor of Muhammad, the Messenger of God (SAWW). With Muhammad prophethood is sealed, and with me successorship is completed and perfected, and I am Amir al-Mu'minin.)) Then he said: Ja'a al-haqq wa zahaqa al-batil: ((The truth has come and falsehood has vanished.))
At that moment, when his entirely generous being set foot on this earthly arena, the idols in the Ka'ba fell on their faces and the heavens were illuminated. Satan cried out:
((Woe to the idols and the idol-worshippers because of this child!))
sources: Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 198.

subsections.title: The Words of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) after His Birth
subsections.text:
Then he greeted the women of Paradise and asked how they were. The ladies of Paradise took him in their arms and the Imam spoke with them. When Hazrat Eve (AS) took him in her arms, he said: ((Peace be upon you, O Mother Eve!)) Eve (AS) replied: Peace be upon you, my son! Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) asked about the condition of Hazrat Adam. Eve (AS) answered: He is immersed in God's blessings and enjoys the favor of his Lord's nearness. While he was inside the Ka'ba, Abu Talib (AS) was calling out in the alleys and the marketplace: Glad tidings to you, for the friend of God has appeared, the one in whom successorship is completed and perfected.
After the women of Paradise left, the divine prophets — Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus (AS) — came. Seeing them, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) stirred and smiled, and those honored figures greeted him: ((Peace be upon you, O friend of God and successor of the Prophet of God.))
In reply, he said: ((Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and blessings.)) And he greeted each of them individually. Those honored figures embraced and kissed him one after another, opened their tongues in his praise and left. Then the angels came and took him to the heavens, brought him back and took him again, and each time they spoke special words about his virtues and merits. Fatima bint Asad (AS) says: The second time they brought him back, he was wrapped in white heavenly silk, and they said to me: ((Protect him from the eyes of onlookers, for he is the friend of the Lord of the Worlds. Know that no one enters Paradise except one who accepts his Wilayah and affirms his Imamate and Wilayah. Blessed is the one who follows him, and woe to the one who turns away from him. His likeness is like the Ark of Noah: whoever joined it was saved, and whoever stayed behind was drowned and fell.)) Then they said something in his ear that I did not understand. Then they kissed him, rose and went out, and I did not know where they left from.
sources: Rawdat al-Wa'izin: vol. 1, p. 79. Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 198. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 13.
Ali (AS) Walid al-Ka'ba: p. 32.
Ali (AS) Walid al-Ka'ba: p. 32.

subsections.title: Three Days in the Ka'ba
subsections.text:
After three days as a guest of God, Fatima bint Asad (AS) took her blessed and honored child in her arms and was preparing to leave the Ka'ba, when an unseen voice called out: ((O Fatima, name this child Ali, for I am God, the Most High (Ali al-A'la). I have derived his name from My own name, I have taught him manners, entrusted My command to him and made him aware of the subtleties of My knowledge. He was born in My House. He is the first to call the adhan from atop My House, and to break the idols and throw them down on their faces from the top of the Ka'ba. Blessed is the one who loves him, obeys him and helps him. Woe to the one who hates him, disobeys him, humiliates him and denies his right.))
During these three days, in every gathering there was talk of the birth of this blessed and exceptional child; in particular, the lock of the Ka'ba door not opening, and the wall of the Ka'ba splitting open in daytime and being seen by the disbelievers, turned this matter into a public issue.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, pp. 9–37.

subsections.title: The Rising of the Light of Ali (AS) in the Arms of the Prophet (SAWW)
subsections.text:
On the morning of the fourth day, while people sat watching in anticipation, the wall of the Ka'ba suddenly split open at the same spot as before, so that Fatima bint Asad (AS) and her dear child came out from there. Everyone was watching, and before anyone asked, Fatima bint Asad (AS) told them about some of the events inside the House, the greatness of that child, the heavenly foods, and that his name, by a heavenly call, is Ali (AS).
Abu Talib (AS) and the Prophet (SAWW) came forward, and Fatima bint Asad (AS) came forward with the newborn. Hazrat Mawla al-Mawali Ali (AS) said: Peace be upon you, O my father, and God's mercy and blessings. Abu Talib (AS) said: And peace be upon you, O my son, and God's mercy and blessings, and took him in his arms. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) opened his blessed eyes toward the face of the Prophet (SAWW), smiled, moved his body and said: Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and blessings; take me in your arms.
The Prophet (SAWW) returned his greeting, took him in his arms, kissed him and placed his hand in his. Then Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) placed his right hand on his ear and recited the adhan and iqama, and bore witness to the oneness of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and to the prophethood of the Prophet (SAWW). Then he asked the Prophet (SAWW) for permission to recite the heavenly books. After the Prophet (SAWW) gave permission, he cleared his chest and recited what was in the scrolls of Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus (AS). Then he began reciting the Qur'an, which had not yet been revealed. He began the blessed Surah al-Mu'minun: Qad aflaha al-mu'minun.... Then, while he was in the arms of the Messenger of God (SAWW), they returned to the house of Abu Talib (AS).
Fatima bint Asad (AS) says: When I came out of the Ka'ba and placed the child with the Prophet (SAWW), he opened Ali's (AS) mouth with his blessed tongue, performed tahnik on him with his blessed saliva, recited the adhan in his right ear and the iqama in his left, and said: ((This is a newborn who was born upon the fitra (natural disposition).))
On the third day after his birth, or the third day after leaving the Ka'ba, and according to some accounts the tenth of Dhu al-Hijja, Hazrat Abu Talib said: ((First circumambulate the Ka'ba seven times, and then greet my son Ali (AS).))
sources: Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 198.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 22. Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 198.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 18. Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 172. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 1, p. 59.
Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 199.
Manaqib: vol. 2, p. 199.

subsections.title: Ali's (AS) Childhood with the Prophet (SAWW)
subsections.text: Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) says about his childhood and his companionship with the Prophet (SAWW): In my childhood, the Prophet (SAWW) would hold me in his lap and press me to his chest. He would chew food and put it in my mouth. He would let the fragrance of his good scent reach my soul. He found no lie in my speech and no error or ignorance in my conduct. From the time of his weaning, God had appointed the greatest of the angels to accompany the Prophet (SAWW), to guide him night and day in the paths of the world's noble and good deeds. And I used to follow the Prophet (SAWW) as a nursing child obeys its mother and follows her actions. Every year he would go to Mount Hira, and at that time no one but me saw him.
sources: Last parts of Sermon 234 of Nahj al-Balagha, Fayd al-Islam edition: p. 802.

events.title: Death of al-Mu'tamid the Abbasid
events.text:
On this day in the year 279 AH, al-Mu'tamid 'ala Allah Ahmad ibn al-Mutawakkil, titled al-Mu'tamid, went to Hell. The cause of his death was that he was indulging in revelry beside a stream, and from drinking too much wine, or from a poison that his nephew had put in his wine, his belly burst; according to another account, he went to his doom on 18 Rajab.
During his 23 years of caliphate, al-Mu'tamid devoted himself to pleasure and amusements, and the affairs of the state were in the hands of his brother Ahmad al-Muwaffaq. After him, his son Ahmad al-Mu'tadid carried on his father's work until he removed his uncle al-Mu'tamid from his path and himself reached the caliphate.
Among the gravest crimes of al-Mu'tamid is the poisoning of our master and lord Hazrat Imam Hasan al-'Askari (AS). Saduq (RH) says: Al-Mu'tamid imprisoned Imam al-'Askari (AS) several times.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 142.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 360.

events.title: Visiting Imam Husayn (AS)
events.text: On the night of 15 Rajab and its day, visiting Imam Husayn (AS), as well as visiting the holy shrines of the Infallibles (AS), is recommended.
sources: Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 307–308. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 741. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 145. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 599.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 35.

events.title: Passing of Hazrat Zaynab (AS)
events.text:
The oppressed and lonely passing of Umm al-Masa'ib, Hazrat Fatima Sughra, the Noblewoman of Banu Hashim, Zaynab al-Kubra (AS), took place on the night of Sunday, 15 Rajab, in the year 62 AH.
For one year after the event of Karbala, her life was spent in tears, sighs and the memories of captivity and Karbala. It suffices for the greatness of that veiled lady that, according to Saduq (RH), she held a special deputyship from Imam Husayn (AS), and this deputyship continued until Imam Zayn al-'Abidin's (AS) illness had passed.
sources: Zaynab al-Kubra (AS) by Naqdi: p. 114. Ma'ali al-Sibtayn: vol. 2, p. 225.
Shajara-ye Tuba: vol. 2, p. 392.

subsections.title: The Naming of Hazrat Zaynab (AS)
subsections.text:
At the time of her birth, Gabriel descended from Almighty God upon the Prophet (SAWW) and said: ((O Messenger of God, name this girl Zaynab.)) Then Gabriel wept. The Prophet (SAWW) asked: What is the reason for this weeping? He replied: Indeed this girl, from the beginning of her life until the end of time, will live in this transient abode with suffering, pain and affliction. At times she will be afflicted with the pain of your calamity, O Messenger of God; at times with mourning for her mother, at times with the calamity of her father, and at times with the pain of separation from her brother Hasan Mujtaba (AS). Above all, she will be caught in the calamities of Karbala and the misfortunes of the plain of Nineveh, so that her hair will turn white and her stature will be bent.
The Ahl al-Bayt (AS) heard this news and became grieved and wept. The Prophet (SAWW) placed his face on the face of Hazrat Zaynab (AS) and wept. Hazrat Siddiqa Tahira (AS) said: O Father, what is this weeping for? May God not make your eyes weep. He said: O Fatima, after me and you, this girl will suffer trials and calamities. Hazrat Siddiqa (AS) said: What reward will one have who weeps for my daughter Zaynab (AS)? He said: ((O piece of my body and light of my eyes, the reward of one who weeps for her and her calamities is like the reward of one who weeps for her brother Husayn.)) Then he named her ((Zaynab)).
She passed away in her own house, a year and a few months after the event of Karbala, with a heart full of grief over the calamities of Karbala, and was buried in the same house. As for the passing of that oppressed veiled lady, 14 Rajab and the tenth of Ramadan have also been mentioned.
sources: Riyahin al-Shari'a: vol. 3, pp. 38–39.
al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. 1, p. 113.

events.title: Change of the Qibla
events.text: On 15 Rajab in the year 2 AH, the Qibla was changed from Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) toward the Ka'ba. This took place during the noon prayer at the Mosque of Banu Salim in Medina, and this mosque was thereafter called Masjid Dhu al-Qiblatayn (the Mosque of the Two Qiblas).
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 35. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 155. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 308. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 151. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 598. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 742. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 98, p. 345.

events.title: Departure from the Valley (Shi'b) of Abu Talib (AS)
events.text: On this day, the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW) left the Valley (Shi'b) of Abu Talib (AS).
sources: Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 741. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 308. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 145. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 599. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, p. 598.

events.title: Martyrdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS)
events.text: According to one narration, the martyrdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) took place on such a day in the year 148 AH.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 514. Rawdat al-Wa'izin: vol. 1, p. 212.

events.title: Departure of Fatima bint Asad (AS) from the Ka'ba
events.text: At the beginning of this day, Hazrat Fatima bint Asad (AS) left the Ka'ba with her son Amir al-Mu'minin (AS).
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 35, p. 8.

events.title: Death of al-Ma'mun
events.text: On Thursday, 17 Rajab in the year 218 AH — or according to one account 8 Rajab, 9 Rajab or 18 Rajab — al-Ma'mun, may God's curse be upon him, at the age of 48, joined his forefathers. The duration of his caliphate was 21 years.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 297. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 5, p. 224.
Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 104. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 4, p. 78; vol. 5, p. 224.
Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 17.
Tarikh al-Khulafa': p. 313.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 297. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 312. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, pp. 69, 180. Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 409. Muruj al-Dhahab by Mas'udi: vol. 3, p. 456.

events.title: Passing of Ibrahim, the Son of the Prophet (SAWW)
events.text: In the year 10 AH, Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet (SAWW), passed away. The mother of this honorable child was Maria the Copt. Ibrahim's age at death was, according to one account, 18 months and a few days, and according to another, one year, ten months and eight days.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 76. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 313. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 747. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 34.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, pp. 185–186. An account of this honorable child's life is given in detail in the supplement to Muharram (Tatimma-ye Muharram).
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 22, p. 152.

events.title: Martyrdom of Hazrat Zahra (AS)
events.text: According to the report of Ibn 'Ayyash, the martyrdom of Hazrat Siddiqa Tahira (AS) took place on this day.
sources: Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 747. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 35.

events.title: Beginning of Yazid's Ill-Fated Caliphate
events.text: On this day, the accursed Yazid took hold of the usurped caliphate. Three days after Mu'awiya's death and burial on 15 Rajab, Yazid came to Damascus, went to his tomb and wept. After that he went to the palace and did not come out for three days. Then, on 21 Rajab, he came to the mosque, went up on the pulpit and delivered a sermon.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 208.

events.title: Abu Bakr's Flight in the Battle of Khaybar
events.text: On this day, during the days of the Battle of Khaybar, the banner was given to Abu Bakr, and upon seeing the enemy he fled and also encouraged his group to flee.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 211.

events.title: The Attack on Imam Mujtaba (AS) at Mada'in
events.text: On this day, at Sabat of Mada'in, using the darkness of night, the accursed Jarrah ibn Sinan al-Asadi struck a poisoned dagger or blade into the blessed thigh of Imam Hasan Mujtaba (AS), splitting it to the bone. From the intensity of the pain, the Imam threw his arms around his neck and both fell to the ground. The Imam's friends killed the accursed man and took the Imam (AS) to the house of the governor of Mada'in, Sa'd ibn Mas'ud (the uncle of Mukhtar). Sa'd brought a surgeon and treated the Imam's wound. On this day it is appropriate to visit him and to curse the oppressors and those who attacked him.
sources: Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 749. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 317. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 35.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 35. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 317.

events.title: Poisoning of Musa ibn Ja'far (AS)
events.text: On this day in the year 183 AH, our master and lord Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) was poisoned in the prison of Baghdad on the orders of the accursed Harun.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, p. 1; vol. 97, p. 202. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rajab, p. 225. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 210.

events.title: Umar's Flight in the Battle of Khaybar
events.text: On this day in the Battle of Khaybar, the banner was handed to Umar, and upon seeing the enemy he fled and also encouraged his group to flee.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 211. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 749.

events.title: The Conquest of Khaybar at the Hands of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS)
events.text: On this day in the year 7 AH, in the Battle of Khaybar, Marhab was killed at the hands of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) and the fortress of Khaybar was conquered by him. In Bihar al-Anwar, 27 Rajab is mentioned as the day of the conquest of Khaybar. When the Prophet (SAWW) went to fight the people of Khaybar and besieged the fortress of Qamus, at first he gave the banner to Abu Bakr to fight them. Abu Bakr went with an army, but when he looked at their champions he fled, and the soldiers returned after him. The next day the Prophet (SAWW) gave the banner to Umar, and he too, out of fear of being killed, returned before reaching the battlefield.
sources: Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 35. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 317.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 97, pp. 168–384.

subsections.title: The Selection of Ali (AS) for the Conquest of Khaybar
subsections.text:
The Prophet (SAWW) said: ((Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who attacks repeatedly and does not flee; one who loves God and His Messenger, and whom God and His Messenger love, and through whom God will conquer Khaybar.)) All the Companions wished that this rank and station would be given to them.
The next day, the Prophet (SAWW) said: Where is Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)? They said: He has an eye ailment, and moving is difficult for him. The Seal of the Prophets (SAWW) said: Bring him. Salama ibn al-Akwa' went and brought him. The Prophet (SAWW) took his head in his lap and rubbed his blessed saliva on the luminous eyes of Hazrat Khatam al-Awsiya Ali Murtada (AS) and said: ((O God, remove from him the hardship of heat and cold.)) After that day, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) never suffered from eye pain and was never troubled by heat or cold.
The Prophet (SAWW) put his own armor on him, fastened Dhu al-Fiqar to his waist, entrusted the banner to him, mounted him on his steed and said: ((Gabriel is on your right, Michael on your left, Azrael in front, Israfil behind, God's victory above your head, and my prayer too is behind you.)) He said: O Ali, offer Islam to them

subsections.title: The Battlefield of Khaybar
subsections.text:
He went, and after exhortation and advice, a number of men came to fight him. They martyred two of the Muslims. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) charged at them and they were killed. Then Marhab's brother came with a group. The Imam sent them, too, to perdition.
Marhab, who was brave, came to avenge them. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) struck him on the head with Dhu al-Fiqar so hard that the sword passed through his throat, split him in two and threw him to the ground. The sound of the Muslims' takbir rose. A group of Jews came to defend and fought the Muslims. Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) continued fighting until some were killed and some fled into the fortress.
With his mighty Haydari hand, he tore off the door of the fortress and made it a bridge for the Muslims to cross the moat. He carried the Muslims across the moat on that door several times, though he had been hungry for three days.
sources: al-Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn: vol. 3, p. 37. Majma' al-Zawa'id wa Manba' al-Fawa'id: vol. 9, p. 124. Kanz al-'Ummal: vol. 5, p. 283. Fayd al-'Allam: pp. 317–321.

events.title: Return of Ja'far al-Tayyar from Abyssinia
events.text: The arrival of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (AS), the brother of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), from Abyssinia took place on the day of the conquest of Khaybar.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 56. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rajab, p. 255.

events.title: Martyrdom of Musa ibn Ja'far (AS)
events.text: On this day in the year 183 AH, according to the well-known view, Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) was martyred in the prison of Sindi ibn Shahak. According to the narration of the late Kulayni, the day of Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far's (AS) martyrdom is the sixth of Rajab. The accursed Harun came to the Mosque of the Prophet (SAWW) ostensibly for a visit, but in truth to arrest Hazrat Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) and send him from Medina to Baghdad.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 6. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, p. 206. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 36. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 749. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 35. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 322. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2, p. 598.
Kafi: vol. 2, p. 507.
Kafi: vol. 2, p. 507. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 48, p. 206.

subsections.title: The Tyrannical Caliphs during the Imam's Imamate
subsections.text: He was 20 years old when the Imamate passed to him, and he held the Imamate for 35 years. During this time, after the martyrdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), he was for some time contemporary with Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, who did not interfere with him. After al-Mansur came nearly ten years of al-Mahdi's caliphate. He summoned the Imam to Iraq and imprisoned him. One night he saw Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) in a dream, who said to him: "Would you perhaps, if you were given authority, cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship?" When he awoke, he understood the Imam's meaning and released Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) from prison. After al-Mahdi, his son al-Hadi wanted to imprison him, but death did not give him respite, as he reigned for less than a year. When the caliphate reached Harun, he sent the Imam (AS) from one prison to another, until in the fourteenth year of his caliphate he martyred him, at the age of 55, with the poison of oppression.
sources: Surah Muhammad (SAWW): verse 22.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, pp. 33–34.

subsections.title: The Washing and Burial of the Imam
subsections.text:
After the martyrdom, according to Harun's order, in order to insult that honorable figure, his noble body was placed on a ladder in old clothes and carried on the shoulders of four porters, while someone called out in front of the funeral: ((This is the Imam of the Rafidis.)) Imam Reza (AS) had previously taken care of his washing, shrouding and prayer. Then the Shi'a came, brought flowers and paid their respects, and buried his body at the present location of the holy shrine.
The number of his children was 37, the duration of his Imamate was 35 years, and the Imam's noble age at the time of martyrdom was 55 years. His martyrdom is also mentioned as occurring on 5 or 6 Rajab.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rajab, p. 279, from Jannat al-Khulud.
Irshad: vol. 2, p. 244.
A'lam al-Wara: vol. 2, p. 6. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 215.
Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub: vol. 4, p. 349. Kafi: vol. 2, p. 507. Irshad: vol. 2, p. 215.

events.title: Passing of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS)
events.text: The Master of Batha', Hazrat Abu Talib (AS), passed away three years before the Hijra, in the 10th year of the Bi'tha. According to one account, his age at the time of his passing was 81 years. Other accounts of the passing of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS) are: 27 Jumada al-Ula, 26 and 29 Rajab, 7 and 18 Ramadan, 15 and 17 Shawwal, the 1st and 10th of Dhu al-Qa'da, and the 1st of Dhu al-Hijja.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 43. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 19, p. 24. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 326. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 284. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 749.
Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 80. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 303, from Bihar al-Anwar.
Nafa'ih al-'Allam: p. 158. Usd al-Ghaba: vol. 1, p. 19. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, p. 284. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 43. Ihqaq al-Haqq: vol. 29, p. 614.

subsections.title: The Lineage of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS)
subsections.text: His blessed name was Imran; his father was Abd al-Muttalib and his mother was Fatima bint Amr ibn A'idh. Abu Talib (AS), Abdullah (the father of the Prophet (SAWW)) and Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib were full brothers, that is, they shared both father and mother, while Abd al-Muttalib's other children shared only a father with these three honorable men.

subsections.title: The Faith of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS)
subsections.text:
Majlisi (RH) says: The Imamiyya are unanimous regarding the Islam and faith of Abu Talib (AS) in the Prophet (SAWW), and that he never worshipped an idol. Rather, Abu Talib (AS) was one of the successors of Abraham (AS), and the matter of his Islam and faith is well known among the Shi'a, and Shi'a scholars have written books on this honorable man's faith.
Saduq (RH) says: It is stated in a hadith that Abd al-Muttalib (AS) was a divine proof and Abu Talib (AS) was his successor. According to the narration, the trusts of the prophets, the staff of Moses (AS), the ring of Solomon (AS), and so on, were entrusted by Abd al-Muttalib (AS) to Abu Talib, who in turn handed them over to the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW).
Ibn al-Athir al-Jazari, a Shafi'i, says: The Ahl al-Bayt (AS) are unanimous regarding Abu Talib's (AS) faith, and the consensus of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) is a proof.
Many books have been written on the faith of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS), the first of which was written in the year 630 AH. Since then, books in various languages on his faith, greatness and eminence have been written and printed, which is not hidden from researchers.
Hazrat Reza (AS) says: ((Whoever believes that Abu Talib (AS) died in a state of disbelief is himself a disbeliever.))
The poems of Hazrat Abu Talib (AS) in defense of the Prophet (SAWW), the verses attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) at the time of Abu Talib's (AS) passing, his words to the Quraysh in the Masjid al-Haram when the Quraysh intended harm toward the Prophet (SAWW), his words at the time of his passing, and his words in seeking rain all indicate that he possessed a unique faith, which in narrations is likened to the faith of the Companions of the Cave. Some of the verses of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) in elegy for him also indicate his superiority over Hamza.
Asbagh ibn Nubata says: Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said: ((By God, my father, my grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, Hashim and Abd Manaf never worshipped idols.)) They said: Then what did they worship? He said: They prayed toward the Ka'ba and held fast to the religion of Abraham.
Ibn Abi al-Hadid says in some verses: If it were not for Abu Talib and his son, religion would not have stood firm in such a way. Abu Talib defended the Prophet (SAWW) in Mecca, and his son in Medina defended and protected the Prophet (SAWW) unsparingly.
sources: Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: pp. 113–114. Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, pp. 286–306. Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 14, pp. 66–85.
Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Rajab, pp. 284, 289, 314, 317, 318, 322.

Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 14, p. 85. And Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 289 states: According to Suyuti, the hadiths that disrespect that honorable man are among the fabrications of the era of Mu'awiya and others, made to please the accursed tree of Banu Umayya, and among their narrators is Mughira ibn Shu'ba, who is famous throughout the world for his enmity and hostility toward Banu Hashim.

subsections.title: The Prophet (SAWW) at the Passing of Abu Talib (AS)
subsections.text:
When Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) informed the Prophet (SAWW) of Abu Talib's (AS) passing, he became deeply saddened and grieved and said: ((O Ali, go, wash him, apply hanut and shroud him, and when you have placed him on the bier, inform me.)) When he had carried out the Prophet's (SAWW) instructions and placed his honorable father on the bier, the Prophet (SAWW) came himself, and when his blessed gaze fell on the body of his honorable uncle, tenderness and sorrow came over him and he said: ((O uncle, you upheld the ties of kinship and showed kindness, and you were rewarded with good. O uncle, you sponsored me in my childhood and in my adulthood you supported and protected me.))
Then he turned to the people and said: ((By God, I will be granted permission to intercede for my uncle on the Day of Resurrection, such that jinn and humans will be amazed at that intercession.)) With the passing of Abu Talib (AS), Gabriel descended and said to the Prophet (SAWW): ((Your helper has left the world; emigrate.))
During his lifetime, Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) used to appoint deputies to perform Hajj on behalf of Abdullah, Amina and Abu Talib (AS), and at the time of his martyrdom he instructed his children to appoint deputies in Mecca to perform Hajj on behalf of those honorable ones.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 19, p. 69.
Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. 1, p. 303.

events.title: The Bi'tha (Prophetic Mission) of the Prophet (SAWW)
events.text:
The blessed Bi'tha of the Prophet (SAWW), at the age of 40, and the beginning of the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet (SAWW), took place on this day.
This day is one of the great Eids, and it is the day on which the Messenger of God (SAWW) was appointed to the mission of prophethood and Gabriel (AS) descended upon him in his prophethood. Non-Shi'a consider the Bi'tha to have been on 17, 18 or 24 Ramadan, and some on 12 Rabi' al-Awwal.
On this day, sending blessings upon the Prophet (SAWW) and his Ahl al-Bayt, as well as visiting him and Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), has been prescribed.
Many years had passed since the missions of the earlier prophets (AS), and every people and tribe lived by its own differing beliefs; in the Hijaz and Mecca of that time, people worshipped many idols: idols of stone, of metal, of wood, and sometimes made of dates. Girls were buried alive. Most tribes were in a state of war and bloodshed. The world was drowned in misguidance and error. Then forty years passed from the blessed birth of the noblest of creation and master of the universe, Hazrat Muhammad ibn Abdullah (SAWW). God appointed him to prophethood, and Gabriel descended upon him and conveyed the divine revelations to him with special etiquette and ceremonies, which are recorded in the books of narrations with various chains of transmission. According to some narrations, when he was returning from Mount Hira, the lights of his majesty and grandeur enveloped him, so much so that no one had the strength to look at him. Every tree, plant and stone he passed would bow before him and say in eloquent speech: ((Peace be upon you, O Prophet of God; peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.))
When he entered the house of Hazrat Khadija (AS), the house was illuminated by the rays of the light of his beauty. Khadija (AS) said: O Muhammad, what is this light that I see from you? He replied: This is the light of prophethood. Then he addressed Hazrat Khadija (AS): Say: ((La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad rasul Allah.)) Khadija (AS) said: For years I have known of your prophethood. Then she bore witness to the oneness of Almighty God and the mission of the Prophet (SAWW).
At that moment he said: ((O Khadija, I feel cold. Cover me with a garment.)) He drew a garment over himself and lay down. A call came from the Almighty: Ya ayyuha al-muddaththir, qum fa-andhir wa rabbaka fa-kabbir...: ((O you who wrap yourself in your garment, arise and warn the people of the punishment of your Lord, and proclaim your Lord's greatness.)) He rose, put his blessed finger in his ear and said: ((Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar.)) Then his voice reached all beings, and all agreed with him.
The Prophet (SAWW) invited people secretly to the One God for three years, and after three years Gabriel came and said: ((Almighty God has commanded that you make your invitation public.)) Then he climbed Mount Safa, warned the people and made his invitation public.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 46. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 750. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 37. Tahdhib: vol. 6, p. 2. al-'Udad al-Qawiyya: p. 337. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 36. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 328.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 36.
Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 40.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 47.
Surah al-Muddaththir: verse 1.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 47.
Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 19, pp. 174–186.

events.title: Departure of Imam Husayn (AS) from Medina toward Mecca
events.text:
On this day in the year 60 AH, Imam Husayn (AS) set out from Medina toward Mecca. According to one account, he left Medina on the night of 29 Rajab. Accompanying him on this journey were the Noblewoman of Banu Hashim, Zaynab al-Kubra, their brother Hazrat Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas, Umm Kulthum, Ali Akbar and other members of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS). The sisters of Hazrat Sayyid al-Shuhada (AS), together with the Noblewoman of Banu Hashim and Umm Kulthum (AS), numbered 13.
Other women related to the Imam included the exalted lady Umm Kulthum Sughra, the daughter of Zaynab al-Kubra (AS), who came to Karbala with her husband, and another, Jumana, the daughter of Abu Talib (AS) and sister of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). Also, 9 female servants left Medina with the Imam and 10 male servants were with him. Several of the wives of Imam Mujtaba (AS), 16 of the sons and daughters of Imam Mujtaba (AS), the family of Muslim ibn Aqil (AS) and other companions and relatives of the Imam were also with him.
The provisions and mounts they carried consisted of 250 horses and 250 she-camels. Of these, 70 camels carried the tents, 40 camels carried pots, vessels and food supplies, 30 camels carried water skins, 12 camels carried clothing, dirhams and dinars, 50 camels carried the 50 howdahs prepared for the veiled ladies, the descendants of the Prophet's family, children, dependents, servants and female servants, and the remaining camels carried various other necessary items.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2, p. 34. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1, p. 435. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44, p. 329.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 329.

From the book Az Madina ta Madina (From Medina to Medina): pp. 77–90. For further information, refer to the books Bayt al-Ahzan by Abd al-Khaliq ibn Abd al-Rahim Yazdi, Qamqam-e Zakhkhar, Ma'ali al-Sibtayn, Abu Mikhnaf, Riyad al-Quds, Bihar al-Anwar, and Tarikh A'tham Kufi.

events.title: The First Congregational Prayer in Islam
events.text: On this day, the first person to pray with the Prophet (SAWW) after the Bi'tha was Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). The Prophet (SAWW) was appointed to prophethood on Monday, 27 Rajab, and on 28 Rajab Hazrat Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) performed the prayer with him.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Ayyam: vol. Rajab, p. 247. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 42. Also adapted from Bihar al-Anwar and Manaqib Ibn Shahr Ashub.

events.title: Death of Abu Hanifa
events.text: On this day in the year 150 AH, Nu'man ibn Thabit, known as Abu Hanifa, the leader of the Hanafis, died in Baghdad and was buried in the same city.
sources: Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 132.
Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 286. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1, pp. 95–96.

events.title: Death of al-Shafi'i
events.text:
On Friday, the last day of the month of Rajab in the year 204 AH, Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i died in Egypt.
He remained in his mother's womb for 4 years and was born on the day of Abu Hanifa's death. It is surprising that al-Shafi'i's father had died four years before his birth, and that at birth he delayed out of respect for Abu Hanifa's life.
sources: Rawdat al-Jannat: vol. 7, p. 259. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 258.
Rawdat al-Jannat: vol. 7, p. 258. Tatimmat al-Muntaha: p. 286.

events.title: The Muslims' Migration to Abyssinia
events.text: In this month, after the Bi'tha, by order of the Prophet (SAWW), the Muslims migrated to Abyssinia under the leadership of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (AS).
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 18, pp. 412–422.

events.title: The Nakhla Expedition
events.text: At the end of this month in the second year, the Nakhla expedition took place.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 19, pp. 175–189.

events.title: Passing of the Najashi (Negus), King of Abyssinia
events.text: In this month in the year 9 AH, the Najashi, the king of Abyssinia, passed away. On that day the Prophet (SAWW) said: ((Today a righteous man has departed the world. Rise, so that we may pray over him.)) At that moment the Najashi's body appeared before the Prophet (SAWW), and he and his Companions prayed over him.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 21, p. 369.
Muntaha al-Amal: vol. 1, p. 93.

honorifics.(SAWW): Sallallahu Alayhi wa Alihi wa Sallam — peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny (the Prophet Muhammad)
honorifics.(PBUH): Peace Be Upon Him (used for Imams, Prophets and other holy figures, male)
honorifics.(SA): Salamullah Alayha — peace be upon her (Lady Fatima, Lady Umm Kulthum, Lady Zaynab, Lady Narjis, etc.)
honorifics.(PBUT): Peace Be Upon Them (plural, e.g. the Ahl al-Bayt / the Infallible Imams)
honorifics.(ATFS): Ajjalallahu Ta'ala Farajahu ash-Sharif — may Allah hasten his noble reappearance (the Imam of the Age)
honorifics.(RA): Rahimahullah — may Allah have mercy on him
